rows.reasoning: After reviewing the group's feedback, I maintain my original score. The extreme discrepancy between the clear geometry in the top-right view and the melted, smeared, and incoherent surfaces in the other views represents a catastrophic failure of geometric consistency. For any interactive use case, where a user can freely rotate the object, this inconsistency is not a minor flaw but a complete failure to represent a stable physical object. The back and bottom of the asset are not just 'low quality'; they are geometrically corrupt.

I am not revising my score. The asset is structurally two different objects depending on the viewing angle: a 'basket of apples' from the front, and an 'unidentifiable organic mass' from the back. A 3D asset's primary job is to represent a single, structurally coherent object in space. This asset fails that test in the most fundamental way possible. The high median score from the group suggests they have overlooked or heavily discounted this critical failure, which from a user experience standpoint, renders the asset unusable.

My score remains unchanged. The semantic content of this object is dangerously view-dependent. The meaning switches from 'food in a container' to 'unsettling biological form' when the object is rotated. This is the definition of semantic inconsistency and is precisely the kind of misleading content my evaluation criteria are designed to penalize. A user would be entirely misled about the nature of the object.

I will not change my score. While one view is passably appealing (if blurry), the experience of rotating the object and witnessing its horrifying transformation is profoundly unaesthetic. The overall aesthetic quality of an interactive object must be judged on the total experience, which in this case is jarring and unpleasant. The muddy colors and distorted, fleshy forms in the failure-case views are visually repellent.

I stand by my score of 0. The asset only aligns with the prompt 'Four ripe apples in a basket' from a single, specific hero angle. As a 3D object, it fails to be a 'basket' from all sides. A true 3D representation must fulfill the prompt from all reasonable viewing angles. Because this asset transforms into something completely different and unrelated to the prompt when rotated, it represents a total failure of text-to-3D alignment.
